title: Saw it or heard it?
goal: Choose between -DI and -mIş: what you saw or know as fact, and what you heard, inferred or found out.

intro.text: Choose `-DI` for what you saw, did or know as fact, and `-mIş` for what you heard, read or worked out: *Ali dün geldi* (I saw him) and *Ali dün gelmiş* (I hear). History takes `-DI`; legends take `-mIş`.

vocab.en: to lie, to tell a lie

exercises.question: You watched the match yourself. How do you report the result?

why.1: *Kazanmış* is for a result you heard or read about, not one you watched.

exercises.question: You read the result in the paper the next morning. Which is more natural?

why.1: *Kazandı* presents the result as something you witnessed or vouch for yourself.

exercises.explain: You found out second-hand, so `-mIş`: *kazanmış*, **Turkey won, I see**.

exercises.text: Dün akşam Ali'yi gördüm. Çok yorgun___. Meğer sabaha kadar çalış___.
exercises.en: I saw Ali last night. He was very tired. It turns out he had worked until the morning.

reject.why: *Meğer* (it turns out) brings in what you found out afterwards: *çalışmış*.

exercises.explain: What you saw: *yorgundu*. What you learned afterwards: *çalışmış*.

accept: The thief got in through the back door.
The [thief|burglar] [came in|entered] through the back door.
The burglar got in through the back door.
[Apparently|It seems] the [thief|burglar] [got in|came in|entered] through the back door.
The [thief|burglar] [got in|came in|entered] through the back door, it seems.
The [thief|burglar] [got in|came in|entered] [by|from] the back door.

exercises.en: He lied to me, it turns out.

exercises.explain: Established history is told with `-DI`, though nobody alive saw it: *aldı*.

exercises.text: Efsaneye göre Hezarfen Galata Kulesi'nden Üsküdar'a ___.
exercises.en: According to the legend, Hezarfen flew from the Galata Tower to Üsküdar.
exercises.explain: A legend you can't vouch for takes `-mIş`: *uçmuş*.

exercises.text: Apparently this story is not true.
accept: Apparently this story was not true.
This story is apparently not true.

reject.why: *Yalandı* states it as known fact. **Apparently** calls for `-(y)mIş`: *yalanmış*.

exercises.question: Which part did the narrator learn from Murat, rather than see?

context.tr: Sabah işe gidiyordum. Yolda Murat'ı gördüm.
context.en: I was going to work in the morning. On the way I saw Murat.

context.tr: Murat çok mutluydu. Meğer dün akşam baba olmuş!
context.en: Murat was very happy. It turns out he became a father last night!

options: That Murat was in the street
exercises.explain: *Baba olmuş*: `-mIş`, news he heard. *Mutluydu* is what he saw.
